chapter: Depression years and New Orleans trumpeters
title: His father's law training and Brownlee's choice of music
summary: Brownlee says his father studied law at Tulane, but music was more attractive to him, and the two men compare family professions.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, see, I review all of this stuff.

Well, I see. Well, it must be wonderful to be able to reach in the archives and pull all this out. That's what I need. I wonder if I could take a refresher course at Tulane. You know, that was my father's album, Mammy. But he's graduated from the law school of Tulane.
Yes. Yes. And I guess Dad coached about eight of the top lawyers of Louisiana. And that's what I... It should have been my album, Mammy.

But the law was a little dry for me. And the unfortunate part that I could sing and play piano. And I was in demand so much that I couldn't see anything else. I had a ball. That's a good time. That's the way I feel.
